messages:
Anya: FYI opened a small thread to align on entitlement-based routing + quota override UX. TL;DR: we want per-tier routing defaults, a console toggle for temporary overrides, and explicit spill rules for when capacity is low. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/entitlement-routing (WIP)

Mike: looked at the PR. API shape suggestion below. keeps it simple for customers and for runtime routing: 
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"tier": "free", "preferred": "cpu-small", "spill_to": "pro", "grace_tokens": 10},
    {"tier": "pro", "preferred": "gpu-rtx", "spill_to": "enterprise", "grace_tokens": 50}
  ]
}
```
Mike: `grace_tokens` = soft allowance before strict quota enforcement. runtime can decrement and emit telemetry.

Sophia: Console UX thoughts: expose a single per-tenant toggle "Allow spillover to higher tier" + a small slider for grace tokens. Need clear language: "temporary capacity spill (incurs higher cost)". Also add an audit log entry when ops toggles it.

Product Ops: must require explicit approval for enterprise customers if spill impacts SLA. For free/pro it's ok to allow automatic spill with notifications. Also we need billing events when spill happens.

Anya: Agree. Also runtime concerns: prefer deterministic fallback order rather than dynamic weighing. Keeps telemetry interpretable. So policy should be an ordered list, not a weight map.

Jake: For telemetry we should emit these metrics: `routing.decisions.count{tenant,tier,route}` `routing.spill.count{from_tier,to_tier}` `routing.grace_tokens.used` and an event stream for override toggles. Dashboards: percent of requests spilled by tier over 24h and per-route latency delta.

infra-bot: canary test for entitlement-routing passed on staging (staging.region-us-east-1) — 120k requests, spill rate 2.3%, avg added latency 12ms. See run: https://ci.redwood/jobs/4141

Mike: Nice. One open design question: do we let tenant-level JSON overrides accept arbitrary `spill_to` arrays (multi-hop) or only single-step? Multi-hop complicates rollback during incidents. I'd push for single-step chain enforced at policy validation.

Sophia: UX agrees single-step. If customers want complex chains we can surface a "routing sequence" advanced editor but default is single-step. Keep the toggle simple.

Anya: Also need server-side validation for cycles. Reject policies where A spills to B and B spills to A. Failing fast avoids surprise during routing.

Product Ops: Can we add a soft quota window? e.g. `grace_window_seconds` so grace tokens expire after X seconds. That prevents token hoarding.

Jake: Good idea. Add `grace_window_seconds` to the API. Telemetry should tag spills with `grace_used=true|false`.

Mike: I'll update the PR with single-step enforcement, `grace_window_seconds` and a validation error message. Also adding a small admin-only endpoint to force-reset grace tokens for a tenant: `POST /admin/tenants/:id/reset-grace`.

Sophia: For console mockups I'll wire a small prompt that requires typing the tenant slug to confirm admin override + record who did it.

Anya: Cool. Plan: Mike updates PR, Jake prepares dashboard panels (staging data), Sophia adds console copy & confirmation UX, Product Ops to write short billing spec for spill events. We'll do a 48h canary window in us-east then expand.

infra-bot: deploy to canary group a/b started by @Anya — canary id: ent-route-2026-01 — monitoring live.

Product Ops: noted. I'll draft billing snippet and post here when ready.

Anya: thanks everyone. tagging @infra-bot when canary finishes for final metrics, then we can ship on monday if green. :thumbsup:
